You can include filtering conditions in a search request so that <include target="milvus">Milvus</include><include target="zilliz">Zilliz Cloud</include> conducts metadata filtering before conducting ANN searches, reducing the search scope from the whole collection to only the entities matching the specified filtering conditions.
In <include target="milvus">Milvus</include><include target="zilliz">Zilliz Cloud</include>, filtered searches are categorized into two types —
— depending on the stage at which the filtering is applied.

If a collection contains both vector embeddings and their metadata, you can filter metadata before ANN search to improve the relevancy of the search result. Once <include target="milvus">Milvus</include><include target="zilliz">Zilliz Cloud</include> receives a search request carrying a filtering condition, it restricts the search scope within the entities matching the specified filtering condition.

The standard filtering process effectively narrows the search scope to a small range. However, overly complex filtering expressions may result in
. In such cases, iterative filtering can serve as an alternative, helping to reduce the workload of scalar filtering.

As illustrated in the diagram above, a search with iterative filtering performs the vector search in iterations. Each entity returned by the iterator undergoes scalar filtering, and this process continues until the specified topK results are achieved.
This method significantly reduces the number of entities subjected to scalar filtering, making it especially beneficial for handling highly complex filtering expressions.

, it’s important to note that the iterator processes entities one at a time. This sequential approach can lead to longer processing times or potential performance issues, especially when a large number of entities are subjected to scalar filtering.

To conduct a filtered search with iterative filtering, you can do as follows:

from pymilvus import MilvusClient

client = MilvusClient(
    uri="http://localhost:19530",
    token="root:Milvus"
)

query_vector = [0.3580376395471989, -0.6023495712049978, 0.18414012509913835, -0.26286205330961354, 0.9029438446296592]

res = client.search(
    collection_name="my_collection",
    data=[query_vector],
    limit=5,
    # highlight-start
    filter='color like "red%" and likes > 50',
    output_fields=["color", "likes"],
    search_params={
        "hints": "iterative_filter"
    }
    # highlight-end
)
